answers.how: The accelerating ball track gives approximately 1206 px/s², so the prior sets a local scale of 0.249 cm/px at about 1.20 m depth. The cup is about 59 px tall; correcting to its 1.210 m depth gives 14.8 cm.
The pen spans approximately 40 px. Applying the acceleration-derived scale and the depth ratio 1.175/1.20 gives 9.7 cm.
The cookie diameter is approximately 35 px. Applying the acceleration-derived scale and the depth ratio 1.182/1.20 gives 8.6 cm.
The notebook is approximately 59 px wide. Applying the acceleration-derived scale and the depth ratio 0.962/1.20 gives 11.8 cm.
The desk spans approximately 355 px. Using the acceleration-derived scale and mean endpoint depth of 0.8605 m gives 63.3 cm.
The slope spans approximately 75 px along its incline. Applying the acceleration-derived scale at the mean endpoint depth of 1.2245 m gives 19.0 cm.
The initial ball diameter is approximately 25 px. Applying the acceleration-derived scale and correcting from the initial slope depth of 1.345 m gives 7.0 cm.
A quadratic fit to the accelerating ball track gives approximately 303 px/s and 1206 px/s² at 1.5 s. Thus its speed is 303 × 3/1206 × 100 = 75.4 cm/s.
